title: Technical Analysis I - Charts and Indicators

submodules.title: 1. What Is Technical Analysis?
submodules.intro: What can a price chart tell you, and what can it not?
submodules.content:
⚡ MISSION BRIEFING: TECHNICAL ANALYSIS
Fundamental analysis asks what a business is worth. Technical analysis asks a different question: what is the price itself doing? Technical analysts study charts of past prices and trading activity to look for trends and patterns. It is a way to read market behaviour, not a way to see the future. All examples are fictional and this is education, not advice.

🤯 WOW FACT:
Many ideas behind technical analysis come from Charles Dow, a co-founder of The Wall Street Journal, who wrote about market trends more than a hundred years ago.

⚡ FINANCIAL INTEL: THE THREE BIG IDEAS
• Price reflects what the market knows: news, hopes and fears all end up in the price.
• Prices tend to move in trends instead of jumping around randomly.
• Human behaviour repeats: fear and greed look similar year after year, so chart shapes can repeat.

⚡ FINANCIAL INTEL: TECHNICAL vs FUNDAMENTAL
• Fundamental analysis studies the business: statements, ratios and management.
• Technical analysis studies the chart: price, volume and indicators.
• Many investors use both: fundamentals to choose what to watch, charts to help with timing.

⚡ FINANCIAL INTEL: THE LIMITS
• Chart reading involves judgment, so two people can read the same chart differently.
• Patterns fail often, and nothing works every time.
• A chart cannot warn you about a surprise, such as a new rule or a shock result.

🍕 MINI CASE: TWO WAYS TO LOOK
Aarav likes the numbers of the fictional Sundar Foods Ltd but is unsure when to look at it more closely. Meera shows him its chart: the price has been climbing steadily for months while more shares trade each week. The chart does not tell Aarav what happens next. It shows how buyers and sellers have behaved, and he adds that to his research.

🧪 TRY IT: FUNDAMENTAL OR TECHNICAL?
Sort these: (a) a company's debt-to-equity ratio, (b) a 50-day moving average line, (c) return on equity, (d) the price making higher lows.
(Answers: a and c are fundamental, b and d are technical.)

💡 CORE TAKEAWAY:
Technical analysis reads price and volume to understand trends and behaviour. It works best as a partner to fundamental research, and it never guarantees what happens next.

quiz.question: What does technical analysis mainly study?
quiz.explanation: Technical analysis studies charts of price and trading activity.

quiz.question: Which is one of the core ideas of technical analysis?
options: Prices tend to move in trends
quiz.explanation: Technical analysts assume prices often move in trends rather than randomly.

quiz.question: Which is a fundamental analysis tool, not a technical one?
quiz.explanation: Debt-to-equity comes from the financial statements, so it is fundamental.

quiz.question: Why is technical analysis not a crystal ball?
options: Patterns often fail and readings involve judgment
quiz.explanation: Patterns are probabilities, and different people can read the same chart differently.

quiz.question: How do many investors combine the two methods?
options: Fundamentals to choose what to watch, charts to help with timing
quiz.explanation: Many people research the business first and use charts to help judge timing.

submodules.title: 2. Reading Candlestick Charts
submodules.intro: How does one small candle show a whole day of trading?
submodules.content:
⚡ MISSION BRIEFING: CANDLESTICK CHARTS
A candlestick is a small picture of what the price did during one period, such as one day or one hour. Each candle packs four prices into one shape, so a row of candles tells a story at a glance. Candlestick charts are traced to Japanese rice traders and are now the most common chart style on trading apps. All examples are fictional and this is education, not advice.

🤯 WOW FACT:
A single daily candle squeezes a whole trading day, with thousands of trades, into just four numbers.

⚡ FINANCIAL INTEL: THE FOUR PRICES (OHLC)
• Open: the first price of the period.
• High: the highest price reached.
• Low: the lowest price reached.
• Close: the last price of the period. Many analysts treat the close as the most important of the four.

⚡ FINANCIAL INTEL: ANATOMY OF A CANDLE
• Body: the thick part between the open and the close.
• Wicks (also called shadows): thin lines above and below the body that reach the high and the low.
• In most apps a green candle means the close was above the open, and a red candle means the close was below the open. Colours can be changed in settings, so check your app.
• A long body shows a strong push in one direction. A long wick shows that price went far but was pushed back.

🍕 MINI CASE: ONE DAY, ONE CANDLE
The fictional Sundar Foods Ltd opens at ₹100, touches a high of ₹108 and a low of ₹97, and closes at ₹105. The candle is green because 105 is above 100. The body runs from ₹100 to ₹105, which is ₹5. The upper wick is 108 - 105 = ₹3 and the lower wick is 100 - 97 = ₹3. Sellers pushed the price down early, but buyers brought it back up.

🧪 TRY IT: READ THE CANDLE
A fictional share opens at ₹200, reaches a high of ₹210, falls to a low of ₹195 and closes at ₹196. Is the candle green or red, and how big is the body?
(Answers: red, because it closed below the open. Body = 200 - 196 = ₹4. Upper wick = ₹10 and lower wick = ₹1.)

💡 CORE TAKEAWAY:
A candle shows open, high, low and close in one shape. The body shows where the period began and ended, and the wicks show how far price travelled. Read candles together, not one by one in isolation.

quiz.question: What do the letters OHLC stand for?
quiz.explanation: OHLC means open, high, low and close.

quiz.question: A candle opens at ₹100 and closes at ₹105. What colour is it in most apps?
options: Green, because the close is above the open
quiz.explanation: A close above the open is usually drawn green.

quiz.question: What do the thin wicks of a candle show?
options: The highest and lowest prices of the period
quiz.explanation: Wicks reach the high and the low of the period.

quiz.question: A candle opens at ₹200 and closes at ₹196. What is the body size?
A candle has a long lower wick. What does it suggest?
options: Price fell far but buyers pushed it back up
The share is certain to fall
quiz.explanation: A long lower wick shows price dropped a lot but recovered, though it is only a hint.

submodules.title: 3. Support and Resistance
submodules.intro: Why does price keep turning around at the same levels?
submodules.content:
⚡ MISSION BRIEFING: SUPPORT AND RESISTANCE
Prices often seem to pause or turn at certain levels. Support is a price area where falling prices tend to stop because buyers step in. Resistance is a price area where rising prices tend to stall because sellers step in. They are zones to watch, not exact lines. All examples are fictional and this is education, not advice.

🤯 WOW FACT:
Round numbers like ₹100, ₹500 or ₹1,000 often seem to act as support or resistance, partly because many people place their orders at them.

⚡ FINANCIAL INTEL: HOW LEVELS FORM
• Support: price fell to a level and bounced before, so buyers remember it as a good price.
• Resistance: price rose to a level and fell back, and holders who missed an exit wait to sell there.
• The more times a level holds, the more traders notice it.

⚡ FINANCIAL INTEL: WHEN LEVELS BREAK
• Breakout: price closes clearly above resistance.
• Breakdown: price closes clearly below support.
• Role reversal: broken resistance can turn into support, and broken support can turn into resistance.
• A move that breaks a level and quickly falls back is a false breakout, so many analysts wait for a close beyond the level, ideally on higher volume.

⚡ FINANCIAL INTEL: DRAWING THEM
Think in zones, not single prices. Mark the area where price turned two or three times, and check higher timeframes first, because levels on weekly charts matter more than levels on a 5-minute chart.

🍕 MINI CASE: TWO LEVELS ON A CHART
The fictional GreenGrid Ltd fell to ₹200 in January and bounced, and did the same in March. It rose and stalled twice near ₹250. Meera marks ₹200 as support and ₹250 as resistance. In May the price closes at ₹258 on high volume. The old resistance near ₹250 may now act as support, but Meera keeps watching, because levels can fail.

🧪 TRY IT: NAME THE LEVELS
A fictional share bounced from ₹150 three times and stalled at ₹180 twice. Which is support and which is resistance? If it then closes at ₹185 on heavy volume, what is that called?
(Answers: ₹150 is support, ₹180 is resistance, and the move is a breakout.)

💡 CORE TAKEAWAY:
Support and resistance mark where buyers and sellers have acted before. Treat them as zones, watch what happens when price reaches them, and wait for a clear close before trusting a break.

quiz.question: What is a support level?
options: A price area where rising prices tend to stall
A price area where falling prices tend to pause as buyers step in
quiz.explanation: Support is where buyers have tended to step in and stop a fall.

quiz.question: A share rises to ₹250 and falls back three times. What is ₹250 called?
quiz.explanation: A level where rises stall repeatedly is resistance.

quiz.question: What is a breakout?
options: Price closing clearly above a resistance level
quiz.explanation: A breakout is a clear close above resistance.

quiz.question: What is role reversal?
options: Broken resistance can turn into support, or broken support into resistance
quiz.explanation: A level that breaks often switches its role.

quiz.question: Why do many analysts wait for a close beyond a level before trusting a breakout?
options: Because quick moves beyond a level often fall back, which is a false breakout
quiz.explanation: False breakouts are common, so a confirmed close reduces false alarms.

submodules.title: 4. Trends and Trendlines
submodules.intro: How can you tell whether a price is moving up, down or nowhere?
submodules.content:
⚡ MISSION BRIEFING: TRENDS AND TRENDLINES
A trend is the general direction of price over time. Analysts say 'the trend is your friend' because moving with a trend is usually easier than fighting it. But trends do end, and the skill lies in noticing when. All examples are fictional and this is education, not advice.

🤯 WOW FACT:
Trends exist at every scale: a share can be in a long-term uptrend while having a down week inside it.

⚡ FINANCIAL INTEL: THE THREE TRENDS
• Uptrend: a series of higher highs and higher lows.
• Downtrend: a series of lower highs and lower lows.
• Sideways: price moves in a range between support and resistance.

⚡ FINANCIAL INTEL: TRENDLINES
• Uptrend line: drawn under the swing lows.
• Downtrend line: drawn over the swing highs.
• You need at least two touches to draw one, and a third touch adds confidence.
• A close clearly through the trendline is an early sign the trend may be changing, not proof.

⚡ FINANCIAL INTEL: TREND LENGTHS
Short-term trends last days to weeks, medium-term trends last weeks to months, and long-term trends last months to years. They can point in different directions at the same time, which is normal. Always say which timeframe you mean.

🍕 MINI CASE: SPOTTING AN UPTREND
The fictional MetroSteel Ltd makes swing lows at ₹100, ₹110 and ₹120, and swing highs at ₹130, ₹140 and ₹150. Each low and each high is above the last, so it is an uptrend. Meera draws a line under the lows. If price later closes below that line and then below ₹120, the trend may be weakening.

🧪 TRY IT: NAME THE TREND
A fictional share has swing highs of ₹300, ₹290 and ₹280, and swing lows of ₹250, ₹240 and ₹230. What is the trend, and where would you draw the trendline?
(Answers: a downtrend, because of lower highs and lower lows. The line goes over the swing highs.)

💡 CORE TAKEAWAY:
Trends are described by the pattern of highs and lows. Draw trendlines with care, name the timeframe, and treat a break as a warning to watch, not an instant verdict.

quiz.question: What defines an uptrend?
quiz.explanation: An uptrend is a series of higher highs and higher lows.

quiz.question: Swing highs are ₹300, ₹290, ₹280 and swing lows are ₹250, ₹240, ₹230. What is the trend?
quiz.explanation: Lower highs and lower lows describe a downtrend.

quiz.question: Where is an uptrend line drawn?
quiz.explanation: An uptrend line joins the rising lows.

quiz.question: What is the minimum number of touches needed to draw a trendline?
quiz.explanation: Two points define a line, and a third touch adds confidence.

quiz.question: A price closes below its uptrend line. What does that suggest?
options: The trend may be weakening, which needs more confirmation
quiz.explanation: A break is an early warning, not proof.

submodules.title: 5. Chart Patterns
submodules.intro: Which shapes do analysts look for on a chart?
submodules.content:
⚡ MISSION BRIEFING: CHART PATTERNS
Over time, price movements often form recognisable shapes. Chart patterns are the shapes analysts look for, because they hint at whether a trend may continue or reverse. Patterns are probabilities, not promises. All examples are fictional and this is education, not advice.

🤯 WOW FACT:
Analysts give patterns everyday nicknames, such as head and shoulders, cup and handle, flags and pennants.

⚡ FINANCIAL INTEL: REVERSAL PATTERNS
• Head and shoulders: three peaks with the middle one highest. A close below the 'neckline' (the line joining the dips) hints that a fall may follow.
• Double top: price hits the same high twice and fails, which may signal a turn down.
• Double bottom: price hits the same low twice and then rises, which may signal a turn up.

⚡ FINANCIAL INTEL: CONTINUATION PATTERNS
• Flag or pennant: a short pause after a sharp move, before the move may resume.
• Ascending triangle: a flat top with rising lows.
• Descending triangle: a flat bottom with falling highs.
• Cup and handle: a rounded bottom followed by a small dip before a possible rise.

⚡ FINANCIAL INTEL: USING PATTERNS SAFELY
• Wait for confirmation, such as a close beyond the neckline or boundary.
• Check volume: confirmed moves usually come with more of it.
• Many patterns fail, so always plan an exit.
• A common rule of thumb projects the pattern's height from the breakout point as a rough target. It is a guide, not a guarantee.

🍕 MINI CASE: A DOUBLE TOP
The fictional Rapid Rail Ltd rises to ₹300 twice and falls back each time, with a dip in between at ₹260. When price closes below ₹260, the double top is confirmed. Its height is 300 - 260 = ₹40. Projecting that below the neckline gives 260 - 40 = ₹220. Meera treats ₹220 as a rough guide, not a promise.

🧪 TRY IT: FIND THE TARGET
A fictional share makes a double bottom at ₹80 with a middle peak at ₹100. If it closes above ₹100, what is the rule-of-thumb target?
(Answer: height = 100 - 80 = ₹20, so the target is about 100 + 20 = ₹120.)

💡 CORE TAKEAWAY:
Patterns describe how buyers and sellers have behaved. Wait for confirmation, check volume, plan an exit, and remember that many patterns fail.

quiz.question: Which pattern has three peaks with the middle one highest?
quiz.explanation: That is the head and shoulders shape.

quiz.question: What does a double top suggest?
options: Price failed twice at a high, so a turn down may follow
quiz.explanation: Two failures at the same high can signal a reversal.

quiz.question: A double top has a high of ₹300 and a neckline of ₹260. What is the rule-of-thumb target after a break?
Why wait for confirmation before acting on a pattern?
options: Many shapes fail to complete, so waiting for a clear break reduces false alarms
quiz.explanation: A confirmed break filters out many shapes that never finish.

quiz.question: A flag or pennant after a sharp rise is usually seen as which kind of pattern?
quiz.explanation: Flags and pennants are pauses within an ongoing move.

submodules.title: 6. Volume: The Crowd Behind the Move
submodules.intro: How many people are really behind a price move?
submodules.content:
⚡ MISSION BRIEFING: VOLUME
Volume is the number of shares traded in a period, and it is usually drawn as bars at the bottom of a chart. Price tells you where the market went. Volume tells you how many people took part in the move, which helps you judge how much to trust it. All examples are fictional and this is education, not advice.

🤯 WOW FACT:
Volume bars show how many shares changed hands, something a price line alone can never show.

⚡ FINANCIAL INTEL: WHAT VOLUME TELLS YOU
• Price rising on rising volume: wide participation, usually a healthier move.
• Price rising on falling volume: fewer people are behind it, so the move may be tiring.
• Price falling on high volume: strong selling pressure.

⚡ FINANCIAL INTEL: VOLUME AND BREAKOUTS
• A breakout above resistance on much higher than usual volume is generally considered more reliable.
• A breakout on low volume fails more often.
• Compare volume with the share's own average over the last 20 or 50 days, not with other shares.

⚡ FINANCIAL INTEL: CAUTIONS
• Normal volume differs a lot from share to share. A small company may trade thinly, so a few orders can move its price sharply.
• Results days and news days create spikes.
• A volume spike shows activity, not who is right.

🍕 MINI CASE: TWO BREAKOUTS
The fictional Jal Power Ltd normally trades about 10 lakh shares a day. On the day it breaks above resistance, 25 lakh shares trade, which is 25 ÷ 10 = 2.5 times the average. Weeks later it pushes above another level on only 8 lakh shares. Meera trusts the first breakout more than the second, though neither is a guarantee.

🧪 TRY IT: COMPARE TO THE AVERAGE
The average daily volume of a fictional share is 4 lakh. Today 12 lakh traded while the price rose. How many times the average is that? Is it a stronger or weaker sign than 2 lakh would be?
(Answers: 12 ÷ 4 = 3 times, and it is a stronger sign.)

💡 CORE TAKEAWAY:
Volume shows how many people stand behind a move. Look for moves that come with more participation, compare volume with the share's own average, and remember that volume supports a reading but never proves it.

quiz.question: What does volume measure?
options: The number of shares traded in a period
quiz.explanation: Volume counts the shares traded in a period.

quiz.question: Which is generally a healthier sign for a rising price?
quiz.explanation: Rising prices with rising volume show wider participation.

quiz.question: A breakout on very low volume is generally...
options: Less reliable and more likely to fail
quiz.explanation: Low-volume breakouts fail more often.

quiz.question: Average volume is 4 lakh and today it is 12 lakh. How many times the average is that?
quiz.explanation: 12 ÷ 4 = 3 times.

quiz.question: Why compare today's volume with the share's own average?
options: Normal volume differs from share to share, so only its own history is a fair guide
Average volume is fixed by law
quiz.explanation: Each share has its own normal level of activity.

submodules.title: 7. Moving Averages
submodules.intro: How do you smooth out the noise in a price chart?
submodules.content:
⚡ MISSION BRIEFING: MOVING AVERAGES
Prices jump around from day to day, which makes the trend hard to see. A moving average smooths the noise by averaging recent closing prices and updating every day. It is one of the most common tools on any chart. All examples are fictional and this is education, not advice.

🤯 WOW FACT:
The 200-day moving average is watched so widely that many traders treat it as a rough dividing line between long-term strength and weakness.

⚡ FINANCIAL INTEL: TWO MAIN TYPES
• SMA (Simple Moving Average): the plain average of the last N closing prices.
• EMA (Exponential Moving Average): gives more weight to recent prices, so it reacts faster.
• Common settings are the 20-day, 50-day and 200-day averages (often called DMAs).

⚡ FINANCIAL INTEL: HOW TO READ THEM
• Price above a rising average suggests an uptrend. Price below a falling average suggests a downtrend.
• Averages often act as support or resistance.
• Golden cross: the 50-day average crosses above the 200-day average. Death cross: it crosses below.
• These are lagging signals, because they are built from past prices and show up after a move has begun.

⚡ FINANCIAL INTEL: THE TRADE-OFF
A short average reacts quickly but gives more false alarms. A long average is smoother but later. In sideways markets, moving averages tend to give many false signals.

🍕 MINI CASE: A 5-DAY AVERAGE
The fictional Sundar Foods Ltd closes at ₹100, 102, 104, 103 and 106 over five days. The sum is 515, so the 5-day SMA is 515 ÷ 5 = ₹103. The next day it closes at ₹108. The oldest close drops out, and the new sum is 102 + 104 + 103 + 106 + 108 = 523. The new SMA is 523 ÷ 5 = ₹104.6. The line has moved up with the price.

🧪 TRY IT: FIND THE SMA
A fictional share closes at ₹20, 22, 24, 26 and 28 over five days. What is the 5-day SMA?
(Answer: 120 ÷ 5 = ₹24.)

💡 CORE TAKEAWAY:
Moving averages smooth price to reveal the trend. They lag by design, so use them to understand direction and not to predict turning points.

quiz.question: What does a 5-day SMA calculate?
options: The average of the last 5 closing prices
quiz.explanation: An SMA averages the closing prices over its period.

quiz.question: Closes are ₹20, 22, 24, 26 and 28. What is the 5-day SMA?
How does an EMA differ from an SMA?
options: It reacts slower than any SMA
It gives more weight to recent prices
quiz.explanation: An EMA weights recent prices more, so it reacts faster.

quiz.question: What is a golden cross?
options: The 50-day average crossing above the 200-day average
quiz.explanation: A golden cross is a short-term average crossing above a long-term one.

quiz.question: Why are moving averages called lagging indicators?
options: They are built from past prices, so signals arrive after a move has begun
quiz.explanation: They are calculated from history, so they follow price instead of leading it.

submodules.title: 8. RSI and Momentum
submodules.intro: Is a price move running out of steam?
submodules.content:
⚡ MISSION BRIEFING: RSI AND MOMENTUM
Momentum shows how fast price is moving, not only which way. The RSI (Relative Strength Index) is a popular momentum indicator that places recent gains and losses on a scale from 0 to 100. J. Welles Wilder introduced it in 1978. All examples are fictional and this is education, not advice.

🤯 WOW FACT:
RSI is usually calculated over 14 periods, so on a daily chart it looks at about the last 14 days.

⚡ FINANCIAL INTEL: THE SCALE
• Above 70: the overbought zone, where price has risen fast.
• Below 30: the oversold zone, where price has fallen fast.
• Around 50: balanced momentum.

⚡ FINANCIAL INTEL: HOW TO USE IT WISELY
• Overbought does not mean 'sell now'. In a strong uptrend, RSI can stay above 70 for a long time.
• Oversold does not mean 'buy now'. In a strong downtrend, RSI can stay low for a long time.
• RSI usually works better in sideways markets than in strong trends.
• Divergence: if price makes a new high but RSI does not, momentum may be fading. It is a warning, not a signal.

🍕 MINI CASE: THE STRONG RUN
The fictional Navkar Motors Ltd rises eight days in a row, and its RSI reaches 82. Aarav thinks it must fall now. Meera points out that the trend is strong and RSI can stay high. She waits to see whether price breaks below recent support before drawing any conclusion.

🧪 TRY IT: READ THE ZONES
RSI readings are 25, 52 and 78. Name the zone for each. Does 78 guarantee a fall?
(Answers: 25 is oversold, 52 is neutral and 78 is overbought. No, a high reading is only a caution.)

💡 CORE TAKEAWAY:
RSI measures the speed of recent moves. Use it to spot stretched conditions and fading momentum, but never as a stand-alone buy or sell button.

quiz.question: What range does RSI use?
quiz.explanation: RSI is scaled from 0 to 100.

quiz.question: An RSI above 70 is usually called...
quiz.explanation: Above 70 is the overbought zone.

quiz.question: An RSI reading is 25. Which zone is that?
quiz.explanation: Below 30 is the oversold zone.

quiz.question: Why is 'overbought' not an automatic sell signal?
options: In strong uptrends RSI can stay high for a long time
quiz.explanation: Strong trends can keep RSI elevated for weeks.

quiz.question: What is bearish divergence?
options: Price and RSI both fall together
Price makes a new high but RSI does not, a warning that momentum may be fading
quiz.explanation: A new price high without a new RSI high shows weakening momentum.

submodules.title: 9. MACD
submodules.intro: How do two moving averages reveal changing momentum?
submodules.content:
⚡ MISSION BRIEFING: MACD
MACD (Moving Average Convergence Divergence) compares two exponential moving averages to show momentum and trend together. Gerald Appel created it in the late 1970s. All examples are fictional and this is education, not advice.

🤯 WOW FACT:
Its default settings of 12, 26 and 9 are the standard on most charting platforms.

⚡ FINANCIAL INTEL: THE PARTS
• MACD line = 12-day EMA minus 26-day EMA.
• Signal line = 9-day EMA of the MACD line.
• Histogram = MACD line minus signal line, drawn as bars.

⚡ FINANCIAL INTEL: READING IT
• MACD crosses above the signal line: a bullish crossover, so momentum may be turning up.
• MACD crosses below the signal line: a bearish crossover.
• MACD above zero means the short average is above the long one, an upward bias. Below zero is a downward bias.
• A shrinking histogram means momentum is fading.

⚡ FINANCIAL INTEL: CAUTIONS
MACD is built from moving averages, so it lags. In sideways markets its lines cross back and forth and give many false signals. Use it along with trend, volume and levels.

🍕 MINI CASE: FADING MOMENTUM
For the fictional Navkar Motors Ltd, MACD is 5 and the signal line is 3, so the histogram is 5 - 3 = 2. A week later MACD is 4 and the signal is 3.5, so the histogram is 0.5. It is still positive but shrinking, which hints at fading momentum. If MACD later falls to 3 while the signal is 3.2, the histogram is -0.2, a bearish crossover.

🧪 TRY IT: READ THE HISTOGRAM
MACD is 2.5 and the signal line is 4. What is the histogram, and is MACD above or below the signal line?
(Answers: 2.5 - 4 = -1.5, and MACD is below the signal line, which is bearish.)

💡 CORE TAKEAWAY:
MACD turns two moving averages into a momentum picture. Watch crossovers and the histogram, but expect false signals when price moves sideways.

quiz.question: How is the MACD line calculated?
quiz.explanation: MACD = 12-day EMA minus 26-day EMA.

quiz.question: What is the signal line?
options: A 9-day EMA of the MACD line
quiz.explanation: The signal line smooths the MACD line with a 9-day EMA.

quiz.question: MACD is 5 and the signal line is 3. What is the histogram?
MACD crosses above the signal line. What is it usually called?
quiz.explanation: That is a bullish crossover.

quiz.question: Why can MACD give false signals in sideways markets?
options: It is built from moving averages, which flip back and forth when price has no clear trend
quiz.explanation: Without a trend, the averages cross repeatedly and mislead.

submodules.title: 10. Bollinger Bands and Volatility
submodules.intro: How wide are the swings, and are they about to change?
submodules.content:
⚡ MISSION BRIEFING: VOLATILITY AND BOLLINGER BANDS
Volatility is how much and how fast prices swing. Bollinger Bands draw a channel around price that widens when swings are big and narrows when they are small. John Bollinger developed them in the early 1980s. All examples are fictional and this is education, not advice.

🤯 WOW FACT:
India VIX, often called the 'fear index', is published by the NSE and estimates how much the Nifty 50 is expected to swing over the next 30 days.

⚡ FINANCIAL INTEL: THE THREE LINES
• Middle band: usually the 20-day SMA.
• Upper band: the middle band plus 2 standard deviations.
• Lower band: the middle band minus 2 standard deviations.
Standard deviation is a measure of how spread out recent prices are.

⚡ FINANCIAL INTEL: HOW TO READ THEM
• Price near the upper band is high compared with recent prices. It is not an automatic sell signal, because in a strong trend price can 'walk' along the band.
• Squeeze: very narrow bands show a quiet period, which is often followed by a bigger move. The direction is unknown.
• Wide bands show high volatility.

⚡ FINANCIAL INTEL: A RELATED TOOL: ATR
Average True Range (ATR) shows a share's typical daily price range in rupees. It helps you judge how far a stop-loss should sit, which the last lesson covers.

🍕 MINI CASE: A SQUEEZE
For the fictional Rapid Rail Ltd, the middle band is ₹100 and the standard deviation is ₹5. The upper band is 100 + 10 = ₹110 and the lower band is 100 - 10 = ₹90, so the bands are ₹20 apart. A month later the standard deviation shrinks to ₹2, so the bands are ₹104 and ₹96, only ₹8 apart. Meera notes the quiet spell and waits for the move. She does not guess its direction.

🧪 TRY IT: BUILD THE BANDS
A fictional share has a middle band of ₹250 and a standard deviation of ₹10. What are the upper and lower bands?
(Answers: upper = 250 + 20 = ₹270 and lower = 250 - 20 = ₹230.)

💡 CORE TAKEAWAY:
Bollinger Bands show whether volatility is high or low and how stretched price is. Use them to understand conditions, not to trigger buying or selling on their own.

quiz.question: What is the middle line of Bollinger Bands usually?
quiz.explanation: The middle band is typically a 20-day simple moving average.

quiz.question: The middle band is ₹100 and the standard deviation is ₹5. What is the upper band using 2 standard deviations?
What does a squeeze (very narrow bands) suggest?
options: A quiet period often followed by a bigger move, with direction unknown
quiz.explanation: Low volatility often gives way to larger swings, but the direction is unclear.

quiz.question: Price touches the upper band. What is a fair reading?
options: Price is high compared with recent prices, but it is not an automatic sell signal
quiz.explanation: In strong trends, price can stay near the upper band for a while.

quiz.question: What does India VIX estimate?
options: Expected volatility of the Nifty 50 over the next 30 days
quiz.explanation: India VIX measures expected market volatility.

submodules.title: 11. Timeframes and Trade Planning
submodules.intro: How do you match your charts to how long you plan to hold?
submodules.content:
⚡ MISSION BRIEFING: TIMEFRAMES AND PLANNING
The same share can look like an uptrend on a weekly chart and a downtrend on a 5-minute chart. The timeframe you pick should match how long you plan to hold. Planning means deciding your entry, exit and risk before you act, not after. All examples are fictional and this is education, not advice.

🤯 WOW FACT:
Indian stock exchanges trade from 9:15 am to 3:30 pm on weekdays, so one daily candle holds only about 6 hours and 15 minutes of trading.

⚡ FINANCIAL INTEL: STYLES AND TIMEFRAMES
• Intraday: bought and sold the same day, using 1 to 15 minute charts.
• Swing: held for days to weeks, using daily charts.
• Positional: held for weeks to months, using daily and weekly charts.
• Long-term investing: held for years, using weekly and monthly charts.
Short-term styles need more time and discipline and carry higher risk. SEBI studies have found that most individual short-term traders lose money.

⚡ FINANCIAL INTEL: THE TOP-DOWN CHECK
1. Start on a higher timeframe, such as weekly, to see the main trend and big levels.
2. Zoom to the daily chart for levels and patterns.
3. Use a shorter chart only for fine timing.
Trading in the direction of the higher timeframe trend is usually easier than going against it.

⚡ FINANCIAL INTEL: THE TRADE PLAN
Write down before you act: the reason for the idea, the entry price, the stop-loss price, the target, and the most you are willing to lose. If you cannot write it in a few lines, the idea is not ready.

🍕 MINI CASE: A PLAN ON PAPER
Meera studies the fictional Pragati Pumps Ltd. The weekly chart shows an uptrend. On the daily chart price is pulling back to support near ₹400, where the rising 50-day average sits. Her plan: enter near ₹405 if support holds, exit if it closes below ₹390, and aim for resistance at ₹440. Risk is 405 - 390 = ₹15 and reward is 440 - 405 = ₹35, so the possible reward is about 2.3 times the risk. She writes this down before doing anything.

🧪 TRY IT: WRITE YOUR PLAN
Choose a fictional share on your simulator and write four lines: reason, entry, stop-loss and target. Then check whether the possible reward is larger than the possible risk.
(Example: entry ₹100, stop ₹95, target ₹110 gives risk ₹5 and reward ₹10.) Discuss it with a parent, teacher or guardian.

💡 CORE TAKEAWAY:
Match your chart timeframe to your holding period, start from the bigger picture, and write a plan before acting. Short-term trading is risky, so practise on a simulator and involve a parent or guardian in any real money decision.

quiz.question: What does intraday trading mean?
options: Buying and selling within the same trading day
quiz.explanation: Intraday trades are opened and closed on the same day.

quiz.question: Why check a higher timeframe first?
options: To see the main trend and big levels
quiz.explanation: The bigger picture gives context for shorter charts.

quiz.question: Which should be decided before entering a trade?
quiz.explanation: A plan sets the entry, exit and risk in advance.

quiz.question: Entry is ₹405, stop is ₹390 and target is ₹440. What is the possible risk per share?
When do Indian equity markets normally trade on weekdays?
quiz.explanation: The regular session runs from 9:15 am to 3:30 pm.

submodules.title: 12. Risk, Stop-Losses and Chart Mistakes
submodules.intro: How do you protect yourself when your chart idea is wrong?
submodules.content:
⚡ MISSION BRIEFING: RISK CONTROL
Every chart reading can be wrong. The skill that matters most is not predicting. It is limiting the damage when you are wrong and making sure good ideas can earn more than bad ones cost. This capstone covers stop-losses, risk and reward, position size and the common mistakes. All examples are fictional and this is education, not advice.

🤯 WOW FACT:
A trader who wins only 4 trades out of 10 can still make money if the winners are twice the size of the losers: 4 x 2 = 8 gained and 6 x 1 = 6 lost, a net gain of 2.

⚡ FINANCIAL INTEL: THE STOP-LOSS
• A stop-loss is a price you decide in advance at which you will exit if the idea is wrong.
• Place it at a level that, if broken, shows the idea has failed, such as below support.
• Decide it before entering, and never move it further away to avoid a loss.

⚡ FINANCIAL INTEL: RISK-REWARD AND POSITION SIZE
• Risk-reward = possible reward ÷ possible risk per share. Entry ₹100, stop ₹95 and target ₹115 give risk 5 and reward 15, so the reward is 3 times the risk.
• Position size = the amount you can afford to lose ÷ risk per share.
• Many traders risk only 1% to 2% of their capital on a single idea.

⚡ FINANCIAL INTEL: COMMON CHART MISTAKES
• Piling on many indicators that all say the same thing.
• Moving the stop-loss after entering.
• Trading without a plan, or too often.
• Seeing only the patterns you hope to see (confirmation bias).
• Ignoring the business and the news.
• Using borrowed money.

🍕 MINI CASE: SIZING A PRACTICE TRADE
Meera has ₹10,000 of practice capital and will risk 2%, which is ₹200. Her entry is ₹100 and her stop is ₹95, so the risk is ₹5 per share. Position size = 200 ÷ 5 = 40 shares. If the stop is hit, she loses 40 x 5 = ₹200, exactly 2% of her capital. The trade can go wrong and still not hurt much.

🧪 TRY IT: SIZE YOUR OWN
Practice capital is ₹20,000 and you risk 1% per trade. Entry is ₹50 and stop is ₹46. How many shares can you buy? If the target is ₹62, what is the risk-reward?
(Answers: 1% of 20,000 = ₹200, risk per share = ₹4, so 200 ÷ 4 = 50 shares. Reward = 62 - 50 = ₹12, and 12 ÷ 4 = 3, so the reward is 3 times the risk.)

💡 CORE TAKEAWAY:
Charts help you plan, and risk control keeps you in the game. Decide your exit first, risk a small part of your capital, and avoid the common mistakes. No tool guarantees profit, so practise on a simulator and involve a parent or guardian in any real money decision.

quiz.question: What is a stop-loss?
options: A pre-decided exit price if the trade goes wrong
quiz.explanation: A stop-loss is the price at which you exit to limit a loss.

quiz.question: Entry ₹100, stop ₹95, target ₹115. What is the risk-reward?
quiz.explanation: Risk is ₹5 and reward is ₹15, so reward is 3 times risk.

quiz.question: Capital ₹10,000, risk 2% (₹200) and risk per share ₹5. How many shares?
quiz.explanation: 200 ÷ 5 = 40 shares.

quiz.question: Which is a common chart mistake?
options: Risking a small share of capital
Moving the stop-loss further away after entering
quiz.explanation: Moving the stop away turns a small planned loss into a bigger one.

quiz.question: A trader wins 4 of 10 trades. Winners gain 2 units and losers lose 1 unit. What is the net result?
quiz.explanation: 4 x 2 = 8 gained, 6 x 1 = 6 lost, so the net is +2.
